intro: MEMO. RE: How this happened. Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honour all of them. Today's roll was seed 1319293479. Please find each roll below, with what the canteen made of it. No action required.

rolls.became: Flo, a seal in a chef's toque, who runs the staff canteen on the fourteenth floor. Clumsy is how the whole thing started: Flo sat on the Igniter 9000, the canteen's wheel-lighting machine, and broke it. There is a seal-shaped dent in the lid.

The canteen's famous dish is real: pasta tossed in a hollowed Parmesan wheel, with a splash of grappa set alight so the inside melts and coats the rigatoni. No flame, no lunch. And after "the incident", Facilities banned matches. The only approved ignition left in the building is a 1958 hand-cranked spark magneto from the basement.

Forty-kilo Parmesan wheels on trolleys. A spark lights one, FWOOMP, the plates go out, and the wheel burns for a few seconds before it's ready for another. A trolley takes four wheels and one spark lights the lot.

The magneto's crank. Drag in circles on it (or tap it, or press space): every full turn throws a spark down the wire to the next dark wheel. If every wheel is already burning, the spark goes pfft. Later the crank gets a mop handle, the Igniter's flint and the Igniter's flywheel, and throws up to four sparks a turn.
The column is a straight line of memos to approve: each one turns up after the one before it, in order. The menu gets better, the crank gets parts, and the floor gets annexed one room at a time.

rolls.value: limited space to arrange (a grid, shelf or map)
rolls.became: The canteen floor. It starts as a two-by-two square and annexes the coat-rack corner, the water cooler, the copier room, meeting room B, the boardroom and finally the terrace, up to six by four. Every spot holds up to four of one thing: wheels on a trolley, pots on a range, interns at a desk. Drag anything to move it.

Where things stand matters. A pasta pot puts more plates out of every wheel beside it (there's pasta to hand), and an intern only relights the wheels beside their desk. So it's a puzzle: wheels want pots on one side and an intern on the other, and the floor never has quite enough room. The glowing spots show what each one would add.
Irene from Accounts pinned a memo to the corkboard: I bet you can't serve 100,000 covers without that machine. Flo has never backed down from a memo. The meter is covers served.

The Igniter 9000, in the corner under a laminated OUT OF ORDER sign. Facilities says the part is on its way. Instead Flo works around it, and then strips it: its flint and flywheel go on the crank, its fan blows on the floor, and its bellows go on the spark wire. The Igniter gets emptier as the canteen gets busier.
Covers, up to a hundred thousand. Lunch vouchers in the thousands. Lighting a wheel serves anything from one cover to twenty-odd, depending on the pots beside it.

About an hour and a half. The first intern turns up about ten minutes in. Away from the game, the interns keep their wheels going at a tenth of the pace, for up to two hours, and leave you a memo saying so.
Irene from Accounts, and her mug with the I on it. She pops in now and then just to look, and never uses a coaster.

Three inks on salmon paper, each a hair off register: shading in halftone dots, flames in fluorescent pink, everything keyed in navy. Bowlby One for the headings, Courier Prime for the memos, Reenie Beanie for Irene's handwriting.
Four colours by Aero: navy, purple, fluorescent pink and salmon. The salmon is the paper; the other three are the inks.

A lunchtime jazz combo in D minor: a walking upright bass, brushes, a little piano and a vibraphone. More players join as the floor grows, and it gets a bit quicker at the rush. Every crank click, FWOOMP and chime is on the same D minor scale.
Everything is a memo. Upgrades are memos to approve. The log says FYI, RE: WHEELS, ACTION ITEM and, once, PER MY LAST SPARK. The pointless purchases are filed as NON-ESSENTIAL.

rolls.value: the small thing was the point
rolls.became: The bet was never 100,000. Irene wrote "1 cover", and her mug did the rest: those zeros are coffee rings, and the comma is a drip. Flo had shut the canteen in shame after the Igniter, and Irene only wanted Flo cooking again. The tiny wheel bought "for scale", too small to light, turns out to be the whole point: Irene orders something light, and Flo lights it for one small plate.

At 100,000 covers Irene comes down with her mug, takes the memo off the corkboard and sets the mug on the first zero. It fits. Then the next one. The clues were up the whole time: the rings on the memo, the rings Irene leaves on the board every time she pops in, and the coaster she never uses.

outro: This memo has been approved. Please do not lean on the wheels.
